init.template: Ask the user which locale they want for this project (pt for Portuguese, es for Spanish, or en for English). Then initialize the `.opencode/` project configuration in the current working directory by running the init script with the chosen locale. The script will detect project languages, suggest LSPs, and optionally configure `.vscode/settings.json`. After init completes, verify `.opencode/locale` contains the chosen language. Then review the generated files.
init.description: Initialize opencode project config with repo context and locale

ocf:plan-feature.template: Break down the feature into steps, identify impacted layers, and register risks and planned work in `.opencode/known_issues.md`.

ocf:promote.template: Promote a tracked issue in `known_issues.md`. Read data from the issue entry — if something essential is missing, handle gracefully without asking: `Base branch:` empty → detect from git; `Reviewers:` empty → default to 1; `Remote:` empty → create automatically. If status is `backlog`: run `scripts/promote.sh <id>` (→ ready, status only). If status is `ready`: ensure `Remote:` is populated (auto-create if missing), then run `scripts/promote.sh <id>` (→ in-progress + branch). Other statuses: refuse with reason.
ocf:promote.description: Promote an issue — backlog→ready or ready→in-progress with branch

ocf:review-branch.template: Read `- Reviewers:` from the issue entry in `known_issues.md` to determine how many Senior Reviewers should perform this review. If the field is missing or empty, default to 1 — do NOT ask the user unless the field is absent. Do NOT read reviewer count from opencode.json. Then run a full PR/MR-style review: analyze `git diff`, use that many Senior Engineer reviewers, identify Critical and Major issues only, validate tests and docs, and register new issues.

ocf:develop.template:
Detect the issue ID from the argument, or from the current branch name (`issue-<id>-<slug>`), or ask only if neither is available. Read the issue entry from `known_issues.md`. Check for missing data and handle gracefully:
- `Base branch:` empty → detect from git (origin/HEAD → main/master fallback), no prompt
- `Reviewers:` empty → default to 1, no prompt
- `Business rules:` empty for `feat` type → warn user it will be blocked by Committer gate later
- `Remote:` empty and status needs it → auto-create via `scripts/create_issue.sh <id>`, no prompt

Then auto-promote based on status:

- `backlog`: `scripts/promote.sh <id>` (→ ready) → `scripts/create_issue.sh <id>` (remote) → `scripts/promote.sh <id>` (→ in-progress + branch)
- `ready`: if Remote is `-`, create it first. Then `scripts/promote.sh <id>` (→ in-progress + branch)
- `open` with Remote set: update status to `in-progress`, checkout/create branch `issue-<id>-<slug>`
- `open` with `Remote: -`: `scripts/create_issue.sh <id>` (→ in-progress + branch)
- `in-progress`: proceed directly
- `in-review` / `in-qa` / `in-publish` / `resolved`: refuse — issue is past development

After promotion, verify the current git branch matches `issue-<id>-<slug>`; if not, checkout or create it. Use the preloaded registry entries to select the matching `development/devs/*` implementation subagent. Pass the full issue context (title, description, business rules, acceptance criteria, location, branch) to the subagent. After the selected implementation subagent finishes implementation, update status to `in-review` and automatically proceed to Senior Review — do NOT pause, do NOT ask the user for confirmation, do NOT prompt about creating an MR/PR. The pipeline is continuous.
ocf:develop.description: Start or resume development on an issue, auto-promoting if needed

ocf:scan-issues.template: Run a deep analysis of the codebase to detect new issues (security, concurrency, architecture, reliability). Create or update `.opencode/known_issues.md`. Follow the issue entry format from `standards/issues.md`.
ocf:scan-issues.description: Deep codebase analysis and issue detection

ocf:commit.template: Create an atomic semantic commit following `standards/commits.md`. Use format `<type>(<scope>): <imperative description>` with `Issue: #<id>` and `Status:` trailers. Ask for type/scope/description/issue-id. Detect the project known_issues.md, construct the commit, run `git commit`, and update known_issues.md status based on trailers. Split if the change covers multiple concerns.

ocf:sync-issues.template: Scan known_issues.md entries with Remote: references, fetch remote issue state via gh/glab, sync status (close remote if local resolved, reopen if mismatch), create remote issues for open entries without remote, and report sync results.
ocf:sync-issues.description: Sync known_issues with remote issue tracker

ocf:sync-jira.template: Run the Jira Cloud reconciliation: `scripts/sync-jira.sh sync` — iterate known_issues.md and, for every issue with a `- Jira:` field, transition its card to the status mapped from the local `- Status:` (statusMap in `.opencode/jira.json`, defaults: backlog/ready→To Do, in-progress→In Progress, in-review→In Review, in-qa→QA/Testing, in-publish→Ready for Release, resolved→Done). Configuration comes from `.opencode/jira.json` (baseUrl, email, projectKey, optional statusMap/authMode) or env vars JIRA_BASE_URL/JIRA_PROJECT_KEY/JIRA_EMAIL, plus JIRA_API_TOKEN (env only — never committed, never logged). Without valid config the sync reports it is disabled and exits cleanly. Sync is non-blocking: network/API/auth failures log a warning and continue; transitions not allowed by the Jira workflow are no-ops with a warning. Report per-issue results and the list of issues without a card.
ocf:sync-jira.description: Reconcile known_issues status with Jira Cloud cards

ocf:archive-issue.template: Move a resolved issue from known_issues.md to resolved_issues.md in compact format. The issue must be Status: resolved. Use close_issue.sh which handles both closing and archiving in one step.
ocf:archive-issue.description: Archive resolved issue to compact format

ocf:maintain.template: Run full maintenance on known_issues.md and prioritization. Resolve `prioritization.md` relative to the project root first (`.opencode/prioritization.md`), falling back to `~/.config/opencode/prioritization.md` if the project has no local copy. First run `$SCRIPTS_DIR/maintain.sh` to detect stale issues (local in-progress but remote closed) and status mismatches. Then for each stale issue, run `close_issue.sh <id>` to archive. Reindex remaining issues. Report what was archived/updated.

ocf:close-issue.template: Detect the issue ID from the argument, or from the current branch name (`issue-<id>-<slug>`), or ask if neither is available. Read the issue entry from `known_issues.md`. The issue must have `Remote: #<id>` and `Status: in-publish` or `resolved`. For `in-publish`: verify the PR is merged — if `- PR: #<n>` field exists, run `gh pr view <n> --json state --jq '.state'`; if not merged, report state and abort. If no PR field, search merged PRs by branch name matching `issue-<remote-id>-*`. For `resolved`: the issue is already archived locally, just close the remote if still open. If the remote issue or PR is valid, run `scripts/close_issue.sh <id>` — this closes the remote issue on GitHub/GitLab (with user confirmation) and archives the entry to `resolved_issues.md` in compact format. Report the result.
ocf:close-issue.description: Close remote issue and archive after PR merge

ocf:check-pr.template:
Check PR merge status for issues. Ask the user for an issue ID, or scan all issues with `Status: in-publish`. For each issue:
1. If the issue has a `- PR:` field, use `gh pr view <pr-number> --json state,mergedAt` directly.
2. If no PR field, search for merged PRs referencing the issue:
   - First try: `gh pr list --search "Issue: #<local-id> in:body" --state merged --json number,headRefName,mergedAt`
   - If that fails (or is ambiguous), list all merged PRs with `gh pr list --state merged --json number,headRefName,mergedAt --limit 30` and filter by branch name matching the Remote ID pattern `issue-<remote-id>-`.
3. If a unique merged PR is found:
   - Add a `- PR: #<number>` field to the issue entry
   - Update status to `resolved`
   - Run `close_issue.sh <id>` to archive to `resolved_issues.md`
   - Report PR number and merge date
4. If no merged PR found, report the PR state (open/closed/not found).
5. For issues without `Remote:` field, skip with a warning.
ocf:check-pr.description: Check PR merge status for issues and auto-archive merged ones

ocf:review-external.template: Ask the user for the MR URL (GitHub/GitLab) or remote branch name to review. If nothing is provided, show usage: `ocf:review-external <mr-url|remote-branch>`. Parse the input: if an MR URL is provided, extract the repo and branch info; if a remote branch is provided, use it directly. Fetch the remote branch and check it out locally for analysis. Then run the review-external subagent to perform a structured review across all senior reviewer domains (backend, frontend, security, data, devops, performance, runtime, mobile, ux-ui, qa), classify findings (critical/high/medium/low/nit), generate a report saved to `.opencode/reviews/review-<branch>-<timestamp>.md`, and optionally post critical/high findings to the MR. Present the report path and a summary of findings to the user.
ocf:review-external.description: Review external branches/MRs with structured report generation

ocf:bump-version.template:
Calculate version bump, update changelog, commit, tag, and publish to main. Steps:

1. Read VERSION file → get current version. Find the latest git tag matching `v*` (e.g. v1.2.0). Compare VERSION with the tag version to determine baseline.

2. Analyze commits since the last tag via `git log <last-tag>..HEAD --oneline`. Classify each commit:
   - `feat!:` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` → breaking (major)
   - `feat:` → feature (minor)
   - `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:` → patch-level
   - No meaningful changes → no bump needed, abort

3. Calculate bump type from the highest classification found. Show user:
   - Current VERSION: X.Y.Z
   - Last tag: vX.Y.Z
   - Commits analyzed: N (list types found)
   - Suggested new version: X.Y.Z + 1

4. Ask user to confirm the new version. They can accept, override with a different version, or cancel.

5. If confirmed:
   a. Update VERSION file with new version
   b. Update README.md version badge (line 3: `**Version:** X.Y.Z`)
   c. Ask user for a one-line changelog entry title describing the changes
   d. Read CHANGELOG.md, prepend a new section after the header:
      `## X.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)\n\n- <user's title>`
   e. `git add VERSION README.md CHANGELOG.md`
   f. Commit: `chore: bump version to X.Y.Z`
   g. Create annotated tag: `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "Version X.Y.Z"`
   h. Push commit + tags: `git push origin <current-branch> --tags`
   i. Create GitHub Release: extract the CHANGELOG section for this version and run `gh release create vX.Y.Z --title "vX.Y.Z" --notes "<changelog section>"`
   j. If current branch is NOT main: create a PR to main via `gh pr create --base main --head <current-branch> --title "chore: bump version to X.Y.Z" --body "Automated version bump."`
      If current branch IS main: push directly (already done in step h)

6. Report the result: new version, commit hash, tag, Release URL, and PR URL (if created).
ocf:bump-version.description: Calculate and apply version bump, update changelog, commit, tag, and publish to main

ocf:backup.template: Run `$SCRIPTS_DIR/backup.sh` with the provided arguments. Ask the user for: 1) source directory, 2) backup name (default dev_backup), 3) whether to create a .zip. Then execute the backup. After completion, report the backup path, size, and exclusions applied.
ocf:backup.description: Create intelligent timestamped backup excluding junk

ocf:discovery.template: Invoke the development/discovery subagent to orchestrate the full discovery pipeline (PO -> CTO -> Tech Lead -> PO -> QA -> PM). Start by asking the user for the feature idea or issue description. Then execute all 6 phases sequentially: (1) PO registers prioritization proposal and drives business rules conversation, (2) CTO reviews architectural alignment, (3) Tech Lead refines with technical detail and defines base branch + reviewer profiles, (4) PO creates user story with acceptance criteria and documented business rules, (5) QA validates testability, (6) PM promotes to known_issues.md with status ready. After completion, the issue is tracked and ready for delivery. If the user wants to proceed to implementation, invoke the delivery subagent.
ocf:discovery.description: Orchestrate full discovery pipeline (PO -> CTO -> Tech Lead -> PO -> QA -> PM)

ocf:delivery.template: Invoke the development/delivery subagent to orchestrate the full delivery pipeline from tracked issue to merged MR. The issue must be in known_issues.md with status ready (or backlog if fully refined) and have Base branch, Reviewers, and Remote defined. Execute all phases sequentially: (6) PM promotes issue and creates feature branch, (7) Developer implements with tests (via develop-router), (8) Senior Reviewers review code, (9) QA verifies quality, (10) Committer verifies gates, (11) Publish Requester creates MR. After MR creation, the pipeline pauses. Phase 12 (Close Requester) triggers only after MR is merged. Do NOT pause between phases 7-11 — the pipeline is continuous.
ocf:delivery.description: Orchestrate full delivery pipeline (PM -> Developer -> Review -> QA -> Committer -> Publish -> Close)

ocf:restart-web.template: Restart the opencode web service. IMPORTANT: `sudo systemctl` needs an interactive terminal for the password prompt and CANNOT be run from inside the agent session — do NOT attempt it. Instead, show the user the exact command to run in their own terminal: `sudo systemctl restart opencode`, and explain it applies the latest config changes (agents, skills, commands). If the nginx reverse proxy is installed (via `setup-web.sh --with-nginx`), also suggest `sudo systemctl reload nginx` to pick up nginx config changes. You may check current state read-only (no sudo) with `systemctl is-active opencode` and report it. If the service is not installed, point the user to `scripts/setup-web.sh` (or `ocf:setup-web`).
ocf:restart-web.description: Restart opencode web service to apply configuration changes

ocf:start-web.template: Start the opencode web service. IMPORTANT: `sudo systemctl` needs an interactive terminal and CANNOT be run from inside the agent session — do NOT attempt it. Show the user the exact command to run in their own terminal: `sudo systemctl start opencode`, and explain what it does. You may check state read-only (no sudo) with `systemctl is-active opencode`. If the service is not installed, report that and point to `ocf:setup-web`.

ocf:stop-web.template: Stop the opencode web service. IMPORTANT: `sudo systemctl` needs an interactive terminal and CANNOT be run from inside the agent session — do NOT attempt it. Show the user the exact command to run in their own terminal: `sudo systemctl stop opencode`, and explain they can bring it back with `sudo systemctl start opencode` (`ocf:start-web`). You may check state read-only (no sudo) with `systemctl is-active opencode`.

ocf:reset-web.template: Reset the opencode web service (clear accumulated session DB and restart). The full reset uses `sudo systemctl` internally, which needs an interactive terminal and CANNOT be run from inside the agent session — do NOT attempt it. Instead: (1) run the read-only preview yourself: `$SCRIPTS_DIR/reset-web.sh --list` (no sudo needed) to show the current session DB size (can be GBs); (2) show the user the exact command to run in their own terminal: `bash $SCRIPTS_DIR/reset-web.sh` (or `make reset-web`), explaining it stops the service, moves the session DB to a timestamped backup in `~/.local/share/opencode/backups/`, clears the log dir, and restarts — auth.json/account.json preserved. Ask them to run it in a terminal and report the result.
ocf:reset-web.description: Stop opencode web, clear session cache/DB, and restart

ocf:setup-web.template:
Install or update the opencode web systemd service. IMPORTANT: `setup-web.sh` uses `sudo` internally (systemctl/tee) and CANNOT be run from inside the agent session (no terminal for the password prompt) — do NOT attempt it. Show the user the exact command to run in their own terminal: `sudo scripts/setup-web.sh --user <user> --bin <path-to-opencode>`, and explain it installs/updates the `opencode.service` from the versioned template. The service file is stored at `$SCRIPTS_DIR/opencode.service` and can be replicated to other machines.

Optionally pass `--with-nginx` (and `--hostname opencode.local`) to also set up an nginx reverse proxy with HTTPS (mkcert). This runs `setup-nginx.sh` which: selects a free HTTP port (80→8080→8081→...), generates certs via mkcert, configures nginx as reverse proxy to 127.0.0.1:4096 with HTTP→HTTPS redirect, WebSocket support, and firewall prompt.
ocf:setup-web.description: Install or update the opencode web systemd service (optionally with nginx HTTPS)

ocf:aibot-notify.template: Post exactly ONE standardized aibot message to a remote issue. Arguments: <remote-issue-id> <message-key> [<pr-number>]. The message-key is one of: success | already-in-progress | already-resolved | not-tracked | cannot-develop. Read the templates from standards/aibot-messages.md, select the one for <message-key>, and substitute {issue_id} (and {mr_link} for success — resolve via `gh pr view <n> --json url --jq .url` / `glab mr view <n> --json web_url --jq .web_url`, with fallback built from `git remote get-url origin`). Detect the remote provider (GitHub -> gh, GitLab -> glab) from the workspace git remote. Then invoke the development/aibot subagent via `task:` with subagent_type 'development/aibot', passing: workspace directory, remote issue id, message key, PR number (if provided) and provider. The subagent posts the message to the remote issue (gh issue comment / glab issue comment) in PT-BR, one message per trigger. Do NOT post anything else and NEVER post the token `@aibot:develop`. Report success or failure; failures are non-blocking.
ocf:aibot-notify.description: Post standardized aibot message to a remote issue

ocf:import-skill.template: Import an external skill from a git repository using the vendor clone strategy. Ask the user for the source: a git URL (`https://github.com/owner/repo`) or `owner/repo` shorthand. If the repo contains multiple skills and the user only wants specific ones, ask which folders (relative to the repo root) to check out as sparse paths. Then run `$SCRIPTS_DIR/skill-vendor.sh add <url> [--sparse <paths...>]` — this clones the repo into `~/.config/opencode/vendor/`, discovers every SKILL.md frontmatter name, and registers each as `allow` in `permission.skill` (atomic write to opencode.json). If the repo is already vendored, run `skill-vendor.sh update <name>` instead. Report the installed path and discovered skill names, and tell the user to restart opencode (or restart the web service) for the skills to appear. Never copy skills into `skills/`.
ocf:import-skill.description: Import external skills as git clones via skill-vendor.sh

ocf:telegram-notify.template: Send a Telegram notification to the user. This is for MANUAL use — agents should use the telegram-notifier skill instead. Read the message from the user. Run `$HOME/.config/opencode/scripts/telegram-notify.sh --title "<title>" "<message>"`. If no title is provided, omit --title. The script loads credentials from .opencode/telegram.env automatically. Report success or failure.

ocf:cv-hub.template: Build the candidate's resume hub from a CV PDF (required) + official LinkedIn export (optional) + optional extras, consolidating into hub.json (canonical AI schema) + README.md in a dedicated per-candidate directory. Ask the user for: 1) the candidate directory (default ~/career/<name>), 2) the CV PDF path, 3) the official LinkedIn export directory if available (Download My Data — https://www.linkedin.com/mypreferences/d/download-my-data, option "Baixe um arquivo de dados maior..."; NEVER scrape linkedin.com), 4) optional extra files. Create the directory structure (entradas/, resumes/), copy sources into entradas/, then invoke the career/cv-extractor subagent via task: with the candidate directory and source paths. The subagent runs pdftotext, parses the LinkedIn export, consolidates hub.json per the canonical schema, validates with python3 $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/validate.py until exit 0, and generates README.md. Never fabricate data; mark inferences [INFERIDO]; keep sensitive data out of the hub. Report the hub.json path, validation result, and next step (ocf:cv-tailor).
ocf:cv-hub.description: Build candidate resume hub (hub.json + README.md) from CV PDF + LinkedIn export

ocf:cv-hub-update.template: Update an existing candidate hub incrementally. Args: <candidate-directory> (default ~/career/<name>). If hub.json does NOT exist, tell the user to run ocf:cv-hub first and stop (this command never builds a hub from scratch). Collect the new information from the user — accepted forms: pasted text (recommended), a new PDF path (extract with pdftotext -layout), a new local file path, or manual key-value edits already made to hub.json. Record a snapshot of hub.json BEFORE any change so a precise diff can be reported at the end. Then invoke the career/cv-extractor subagent via task: with the candidate directory, the explicit update-mode instruction, and the new information. The subagent loads the cv-hub skill (update mode): merges the new entries into the EXISTING hub.json — ADD or UPDATE only, NEVER delete an existing entry without the user's explicit confirmation (propose deletions, never apply them silently); detects and merges duplicates (same company+title+start_date in experience, same name in skills/certifications/projects); preserves existing [INFERIDO] markers on entries that had them; marks new inferences [INFERIDO] — never recreates hub.json from scratch. Then validate with python3 $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/validate.py hub.json until exit 0 and regenerate README.md from the updated hub.json (the README is a mirror, never edited manually). Report to the user: the diff/summary of changes (entries added, updated, merged as duplicates, preserved), the validation result, and the regenerated README.md path.
ocf:cv-hub-update.description: Update an existing candidate hub incrementally (add/update entries without recreating hub.json)

ocf:cv-tailor.template: Generate a job-tailored resume PDF from the candidate's hub. Args: <candidate-directory> <job>. The job may be: pasted job description text (recommended), a local file (txt/html/pdf), official LinkedIn export files, or a URL — never fetched: ask the user to paste the job description text instead (URL fetching is removed — LinkedIn always blocks it and redirects may point to file://, an SSRF vector). Validate the hub with python3 $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/validate.py first; if missing, tell the user to run ocf:cv-hub. Then invoke the career/cv-tailor subagent via task: with the candidate directory and job. The subagent: analyzes the job (required/desirable requirements, keywords, seniority, language), performs gap analysis vs hub (saved to resumes/<slug>/gap-analysis.md), lists ALL inferences in resumes/<slug>/inferences.md and asks the candidate to decide on each (rephrase/omit/promote with real data) BEFORE generating the final output, adapts content — reorder/highlight/condense ONLY what exists in the hub, NEVER fabricate, NEVER [INFERIDO] in the final HTML/PDF (internal artifacts only) — in the job's language, generates index.html starting from the reference template skills/career/cv-pdf/templates/resume.html per the standards/cv-design.md design standard (never writes CSS from scratch), verifies ATS/print/page-count conformity against the standard's checklist before generating the PDF, runs the MANDATORY gate bash $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/check-inference.sh index.html (must exit 0 before proceeding), and produces the PDF via bash $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/pdf.sh (Chrome headless A4, fallback LibreOffice). Report the PDF path, gap analysis summary, and the resolved inferences (rephrased/omitted/promoted) the candidate approved — no [INFERIDO] markers in the shareable artifact.
ocf:cv-tailor.description: Generate job-tailored resume PDF from candidate hub

ocf:cv-optimize.template: Analyze a candidate's profile and generate an improvement plan. Args: <candidate-directory> (default ~/career/<name>). If hub.json does not exist or is invalid, first run the ocf:cv-hub flow (ask the user for the CV PDF path, official LinkedIn export if available, and extras), then continue. Validate with python3 $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/validate.py (exit 0 required). Then invoke the career/cv-optimizer subagent via task: with the candidate directory. The subagent produces profile-analysis.md (NO metadata header such as "Generated on:", "Source:", "Tool:", "Note:" — start directly with content; [INFERIDO] markers are inline, not a top banner; the report is written in the user's communication language — session locale or explicit user instruction, English as the fallback) containing: profile score (0-100 per section + global, with textual justification), general qualifications (inferred seniority, top skills, strengths/weaknesses — skill years computed DYNAMICALLY as current year minus the skill's since field when present, never a stale fixed years_of_experience), target job profiles (offline — NEVER concrete jobs/companies/URLs), market salary ranges CLT vs PJ (ALL marked [INFERIDO] for human review, no fabricated sources), context gaps in the hub (missing metrics, unlinked projects, certifications without validity, informal language levels, skills without since/years), and a prioritized action plan (impact x effort, P1-P3). Also render profile-analysis.html and generate profile-analysis.pdf via bash $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/pdf.sh (A4) for easier reading. Never fabricate data; never modify hub.json (report only); no sensitive data in the report. Report the report paths (.md and .pdf), global score, top actions, and [INFERIDO] items to review.
ocf:cv-optimize.description: Analyze candidate profile and generate improvement plan (profile-analysis.md + PDF)

ocf:cv-cover-letter.template: Generate a job-tailored cover letter PDF from the candidate's hub. Args: <candidate-directory> <job>. The job may be: pasted job description text (recommended), a local file (txt/html/pdf), official LinkedIn export files, or a URL (try curl -L respecting robots; LinkedIn always blocks — ask for pasted text, never bypass anti-bot). Validate the hub with python3 $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/validate.py first; if missing, tell the user to run ocf:cv-hub. Then invoke the career/cv-cover-letter subagent via task: with the candidate directory and job. The subagent: analyzes the job (required/desirable requirements, keywords, seniority, language, company profile), reuses the gap analysis from cv-tailor (resumes/<slug>/gap-analysis.md) when available or builds it inline (saved to cartas/<slug>/gap-analysis.md), lists ALL inferences in cartas/<slug>/inferences.md and asks the candidate to decide on each (rephrase/omit/promote with real data) BEFORE generating the final output, drafts the letter — highlighting SPECIFIC hub achievements that match the job's key requirements, NEVER fabricate, NEVER [INFERIDO] in the final HTML/PDF (internal artifacts only) — in the job's language, generates index.html starting from the reference template skills/career/cv-pdf/templates/resume.html per the standards/cv-design.md design standard (never writes CSS from scratch), verifies ATS/print/page-count conformity against the standard's checklist before generating the PDF, runs the MANDATORY gate bash $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/check-inference.sh index.html (must exit 0 before proceeding), and produces the PDF via bash $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/pdf.sh index.html carta-apresentacao.pdf (Chrome headless A4, fallback LibreOffice). Output goes to ~/career/<candidate>/cartas/<job-slug>/ (index.html + carta-apresentacao.pdf). Report the PDF path, gap analysis summary (reused or inline), and the resolved inferences (rephrased/omitted/promoted) the candidate approved — no [INFERIDO] markers in the shareable artifact.
ocf:cv-cover-letter.description: Generate job-tailored cover letter PDF from candidate hub

ocf:cv-linkedin.template: Generate LinkedIn profile optimization suggestions from the candidate's hub. Args: <candidate-directory> [<job>]. The optional job may be: pasted job description text (recommended), a local file (txt/html/pdf), or official LinkedIn export files — NEVER a URL (linkedin.com is never scraped; if the user pastes a URL, ask for pasted text). Validate the hub with python3 $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/validate.py first; if missing, tell the user to run ocf:cv-hub. Then invoke the career/cv-linkedin subagent via task: with the candidate directory and the job (when provided). The subagent: determines the target role — job provided: analyze its requirements/keywords/seniority; no job: read the target job profiles and inferred seniority from ~/career/<candidate>/profile-analysis.md (cv-optimizer) when available, else infer from the hub — then generates the four LinkedIn suggestion blocks: headline (≤220 chars), about section (≤2600 chars), skills ranking (top 50 ranked by relevance to the target role) and featured section recommendations — using ONLY real hub data, in the user's communication language (per standards/cv-analysis.md §1), NEVER fabricating, NEVER scraping or modifying linkedin.com (the user copies/pastes the suggestions manually), with NO [INFERIDO] in the output file (actionable suggestion file, same rule as final resume PDFs per standards/cv-analysis.md §5). Output: ~/career/<candidate>/linkedin-optimization.md following the standards/cv-analysis.md structure (exactly one H1 title, NO metadata header, start directly with content). Report the output path, the target role used, and a summary of the four blocks (headline length, about length, ranked skills count ≤50, featured items count) — no [INFERIDO] markers in the shareable suggestion file.
ocf:cv-linkedin.description: Generate LinkedIn profile optimization suggestions from candidate hub

ocf:cv-interview-prep.template: Generate a structured interview preparation kit from the candidate's hub. Args: <candidate-directory> <job>. The job may be: pasted job description text (recommended), a local file (txt/html/pdf), or official LinkedIn export files — NEVER a URL (linkedin.com is never scraped; if the user pastes a URL, ask for pasted text). Validate the hub with python3 $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/validate.py first; if missing, tell the user to run ocf:cv-hub. Then invoke the career/cv-interview-prep subagent via task: with the candidate directory and the job. The subagent: analyzes the job (required/desirable requirements, keywords/technologies, seniority, languages) to derive the role, then generates the interview preparation kit — likely behavioral and technical questions (role-appropriate), suggested STAR-format answers mapped to REAL hub entries (experience achievements, project impact, certifications, summary), questions to ask the interviewer, technical topics to review (have from the hub vs gap topics), and a preparation gaps section flagging every question/requirement the hub cannot evidence — using ONLY real hub data, in the user's communication language (per standards/cv-analysis.md §1), NEVER fabricating experience, with NO [INFERIDO] in the output file (actionable preparation file, same rule as final resume PDFs per standards/cv-analysis.md §5). Output: ~/career/<candidate>/interview-preparation.md following the standards/cv-analysis.md structure (exactly one H1 title, NO metadata header, start directly with content; H2 sections: Target role, Likely interview questions, Suggested STAR answers, Questions to ask the interviewer, Technical topics to review, Preparation gaps). Report the output path, the target role used, and a summary of the kit (question count by type, STAR answers count, topics to review count, preparation gaps count) — no [INFERIDO] markers in the actionable preparation file.
ocf:cv-interview-prep.description: Generate a structured interview preparation kit from candidate hub

ocf:cv-ats-score.template: Score a generated resume's ATS compatibility. Args: <candidate-directory> <job-slug>. The candidate must have a resume generated by ocf:cv-tailor at ~/career/<candidate>/resumes/<job-slug>/ (curriculo.pdf + index.html + gap-analysis.md). Validate the hub with python3 $SCRIPTS_DIR/cv/validate.py first; if missing, tell the user to run ocf:cv-hub. If the resume artifacts are missing, tell the user to run ocf:cv-tailor for the job slug first. Then invoke the career/cv-ats-score subagent via task: with the candidate directory and the job slug. The subagent: loads the job keywords from resumes/<job-slug>/gap-analysis.md (Job context + Required/Desirable requirements), extracts the resume text from curriculo.pdf via pdftotext (best-effort — if pdftotext is unavailable, report the limitation and fall back to the index.html text; no source → cannot-analyze outcome, never an invented score), computes keyword density (job keywords found vs total, per-keyword counts), detects ATS red flags (tables, images as text, multi-column layouts, missing standard sections — contact, experience, education, skills), scores the resume 0-100 with breakdown keyword_match (40%), section_completeness (30%), format_compliance (30%) plus the weighted global total, and produces actionable recommendations (e.g. "Add 'Kubernetes' to the skills section — it appears 5x in the job but 0x in your resume"). The analysis is computed from the ACTUAL files — NEVER fabricate counts, scores, flags or recommendations. Output: ~/career/<candidate>/resumes/<job-slug>/ats-score.md in the user's communication language (per standards/cv-analysis.md §1) following the standards/cv-analysis.md structure (exactly one H1 title, NO metadata header, start directly with content; canonical score table per §4.2; H2 sections: Job context, ATS score, Keyword density, ATS red flags, Recommendations; [INFERIDO] markers allowed inline in this internal analysis report per §5 — never in the shareable resume artifacts). The agent is read-only besides the report: it NEVER modifies hub.json, gap-analysis.md, inferences.md, index.html or curriculo.pdf. Report the output path, the global score, the breakdown (keyword_match/section_completeness/format_compliance), the text source used, and the count of recommendations.
ocf:cv-ats-score.description: Score a generated resume's ATS compatibility (keyword match, sections, format)
